title: Looks closed, isn't (escalate)
note: A capable chest CT was performed in-window but never mentions the left-upper-lobe nodule. Order-matching would close this; acknowledgment-gated reconciliation escalates it.

reports.full_text:
EXAM: CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST
DATE: 2024-10-08
HISTORY: 58-year-old with remote tobacco use; evaluation for pulmonary nodule.

TECHNIQUE: Helical non-contrast CT of the chest with axial acquisition and coronal/sagittal reconstructions.

FINDINGS:
Lungs: A solid 9 mm nodule is present in the left upper lobe. No prior imaging is available for comparison. No additional suspicious pulmonary nodules. No consolidation.
Mediastinum: No lymphadenopathy. Normal heart size.
Pleura: No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion.

IMPRESSION:
1. Solid 9 mm nodule in the left upper lobe, indeterminate in the absence of priors. Recommend follow-up CT chest in 6 months to assess for interval change.

EXAM: CT ANGIOGRAM, CHEST (PE PROTOCOL)
DATE: 2025-03-18
HISTORY: 58-year-old with acute shortness of breath and cough; rule out pulmonary embolism.

TECHNIQUE: CT angiography of the chest performed with intravenous contrast, pulmonary embolism protocol.

FINDINGS:
Pulmonary arteries: No filling defect to suggest pulmonary embolism.
Lungs: Mild bronchial wall thickening. No lobar consolidation. No pleural effusion.
Heart/mediastinum: Normal cardiac silhouette. No pericardial effusion.

IMPRESSION:
No acute pulmonary embolism. Mild bronchial wall thickening compatible with bronchitis. No pleural effusion.
